parents.source: router task text (repo=phantom, P0, tier=frontier, pool=codex-cmp)
parents.scope: Design the fleet queueing-network model and split it into child jobs covering schema, emitters, estimator, controller, LP/bandit feed, desktop graph and tests. The queueing-network model: job classes by (sourceKind, tierRequirement, effortBand); nodes backlog, lane:<laneId> G/G/c servers with capacity-window vacations and presence caps, hold:{park,cooldown,demote} delay nodes, hold:split absorbing fail state, verify queue, serial merge gates G1b..G7, owner review, and landed/rejected/reverted/dropped/quarantined sinks; routing matrix estimated per (class, lane) route; estimators for arrival rate, service rate, transition probabilities and lane availability with null=unknown honesty; advisory controller recommending admission and slot allocation; metadata-only LP/bandit feed; desktop graph rendering; replay-simulation and conformance tests; flag-gated integration.

externalPrerequisites.acceptance: Router owner confirms ID uniqueness against the live queue and records these children as dispatched; the manifest is a proposed backlog, not proof of enqueue. Reuse delivered work instead of dispatching duplicates.

Changes to protected routing, dispatch, backpressure, merge-gate and daemon paths require an owner-authorized job; manifest entries that name those paths do not authorize editing them under the current job rules.
Enabling any foundry.qnet.* flag beyond shadow observe-only mode requires an owner decision after replay and shadow evidence; no child may self-promote advisory output into live routing.

sharedAcceptance: One self-contained, mergeable change per child with no commits, pushes, tags, releases or edits to protected paths under the current job rules.
Use a temporary HOME for tests, synthetic secret fixtures only, Phantom Secrets for secret delivery and Locus for account/MCP/CLI access.
Run npm run typecheck, npm run lint, npm run check:docs and the child testFiles with npx vitest run; run npm run test:web for src/web-ui changes.
Record commands, pass/fail counts, net LOC, source revision and toolsUsed in BRIDGE_NOTES.md.
Queue telemetry is metadata-only: allowlisted ids, enums, counts and timestamps; never prompt text, diffs, paths, argv, stdout, stderr, environment or secret material.
The queueing model is advisory: it never mutates routing, dispatch, budgets, backlog or authority; flag-off restores byte-identical legacy behaviour; unknown inputs stay unknown (null), never zero.
Unreadable or hostile sources mark the affected estimates degraded rather than fabricating quiet queues; fail closed on identity and authority questions.
Reconcile existing work before dispatch; only the established publisher may push after a separately authorized handoff.

jobs.title: Define the qnet.v1 queue-network schema and contract
acceptance: Define qnet.v1 node kinds (backlog, lane, hold, verify, gate, review, sink), job class (sourceKind, tierRequirement, effortBand), edge kinds, server counts, disciplines and the vacation/availability field per workplans/2026-10-26-queue-network/model.md.
Validation rejects duplicate node ids, dangling edges, unknown kinds, negative server counts and malformed class tuples; errors identify fields without echoing attacker-controlled values.
Golden fixture serializes deterministically; schema version is explicit and unknown versions fail closed.

jobs.title: Project live fleet state into a qnet.v1 snapshot
acceptance: Map backlog items, lane slots and current holds, waiting verifications, open proposals and gate state onto qnet.v1 nodes with per-input sourceState (healthy/degraded/unavailable), reusing existing read-*Detailed readers rather than new file access.
A missing or malformed source degrades only the nodes it feeds; the projection distinguishes an empty healthy queue from an unreadable one and fabricates no depths.
Projection is read-only and pure over injected reads: no dispatch, no ledger writes, no model calls; identity fields stay at the existing hashed-accountHint granularity.

jobs.title: Emit bounded qnet.v1 queue events at network edges
acceptance: Define the event kinds arrive, enqueue, dispatch, hold, release, depart, verify-enter, verify-leave, gate-verdict, land, reject, revert and expire with the allowlisted field set from model.md (schema id, kind, timestamp, item id + class, node id, lane category, post-event queue depth, bounded correlation id).

Append into a per-day bounded ledger under ASHLR_HOME with the same fail-soft never-throw, private-permission discipline as dispatch-production-ledger; corrupt tails degrade reads instead of poisoning the stream.
Provide pure classification helpers so call sites in intake, dispatch, verify and gate code emit exactly one event per transition; duplicate and out-of-order events are detectable by the reader.

jobs.title: Estimate arrival, service and routing parameters
acceptance: Produce per-(class, lane) arrival rates (windowed EWMA), service-time percentiles, transition probabilities and the lane availability schedule a_i(t) from headroom windows, with explicit identifiability labels identified/pooled/insufficient.
Insufficient cohorts yield null, never zero or silently global estimates; unreadable event history marks estimates degraded rather than quiet.
Functions are pure over injected samples and clock; reuse the percentile machinery of src/core/routing/work-estimates.ts semantics rather than duplicating percentile code.

jobs.title: Compute network metrics over the analytic model
acceptance: Compute per-node utilization, expected queue number, mean wait and cycle time, per-lane and per-class throughput, rework amplification and the Little's-law residual health metric using a GI/G/c approximation with observed coefficient of variation plus explicit delay-node semantics for holds.
Flag nodes at or above rho = 1 as unstable rather than reporting infinite waits as numbers; vacationing lanes report suspended availability with their known reopening time.
Every computed metric carries the identifiability and sourceState of its inputs; a degraded input degrades only dependent metrics.

jobs.title: Advisory queueing controller for admission and slots
acceptance: Evaluate a pure function (snapshot, estimates, policy) -> recommendations covering admit/hold per class, per-lane suggested server counts under the availability schedule, and reroute suggestions away from vacationing or demoted lanes; every recommendation carries reasons and the inputs it used.
Enforce the precedence kill-switch and holds > backpressure brakes > budget policy > qnet advice inside the controller itself, so downstream saturation early-holds intake the fixed brakes cannot see.
The controller mutates nothing: recommendations are data; applying them is owned by the flag-gated integration job, and flag-off output is an empty recommendation set.

jobs.title: Export the LP and bandit feed for route allocation
acceptance: Emit a per-epoch normalized export: reward vector per (route, class) of landedPerHour, usdPerLanded, pSuccess and reworkRate with identifiability tags, plus constraint rows for slot bounds, window reserves, per-repo open-PR caps, verify capacity and budget caps.

Solve the bounded allocation LP max r.x s.t. Ax <= b with a small deterministic in-repo solver over fixture sizes; the solver input rejects NaN, negative capacities and unbounded directions instead of producing junk allocations.

Export bandit context (class, availability, utilization, brake state) and realized landed-per-attempt rewards as a metadata-only stream; promotion of any learned weight into live routing is documented as human-gated and stays unimplemented here.

jobs.title: Expose queue status through CLI and FleetStatus
acceptance: phm queue status --json emits one deterministic qnet.v1 view: nodes with depths and utilization, engaged brakes, lane availability and identifiability/degradation labels; --help exits 0 without acting on HOME state.
FleetStatus gains a bounded qnet field sourced from the projection, with absent, malformed and unavailable inputs rendered distinctly from a healthy empty network.
The command performs no dispatch, emission or mutation; doc-facts coverage is updated for the new command and flags.

jobs.title: Render the queue network in the console desktop surface
acceptance: Render one node per queue with WIP badge and utilization ring, edges whose width follows measured flow, suspended lanes with reopening times, and brakes as engaged/idle behind a query flag that defaults off, consistent with the existing Fleet graph approach.
Degraded and unavailable source states are rendered explicitly with omission counts; the view never fabricates a quiet queue and starts no work or extra reads beyond existing polling.
Keyboard-focusable controls, SVG edges with accessible names, bounded node rendering and empty states are covered by the web test suite via npm run test:web.

jobs.title: Replay recorded queues in a discrete-event simulator
acceptance: Implement a deterministic discrete-event replay over the qnet.v1 event stream that reconstructs per-node queue depth, wait times and hold durations without wall-clock sleeps or randomness (seeded inputs only).
Compare model predictions against replayed realized metrics and emit a calibration report bounded to counts and rates; disagreement beyond stated tolerances is reported, never smoothed over.
Replay is read-only over fixture and recorded ledgers and fails closed on corrupt, non-monotonic or hostile event streams.

jobs.title: Conformance suite for telemetry privacy and fail-closed behaviour
acceptance: Assert the emitted event stream contains only allowlisted fields using synthetic sentinel secrets, prompts and paths that must never appear in any record, projection, export or status surface.
Exercise hostile inputs: malformed ledger rows, reversed timestamps, absurd queue depths, unknown node ids and injected fields; each fails closed or is degraded without contaminating healthy nodes.
Prove flag-off equivalence: with qnet disabled the daemon-facing surfaces are byte-identical to legacy behaviour, and no code path reachable from tests mutates routing, budgets or authority.

jobs.title: Wire shadow-mode integration behind foundry.qnet flags
acceptance: Wire emitters, projection, estimator, model and controller into the daemon tick in shadow observe-only mode behind foundry.qnet.* flags that default off; shadow records advice beside the actual decision without influencing it.

Touch protected dispatch and status seams only under the owner-authorized job this entry requires; flag-off restores byte-identical behaviour and leaves all persisted qnet state unread by production paths.
Ship rollback evidence: replay fixtures over crash, duplicate-event and flag-flip sequences showing zero unauthorized dispatches, zero fabricated metrics and a clean revert to legacy routing.
